blogs.title: Semaglutide Myopathy: The Next Safety Signal in the GLP-1 Boom?
blogs.description: With the exponential rise in GLP-1 receptor agonist use for obesity and diabetes, clinicians must stay alert for novel adverse effects. This post discusses the first reported case of immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM) following a single dose of semaglutide, contrasting it with known GI side effects and recent reports of tirzepatide-associated rhabdomyolysis. We explore the implications for pharmacovigilance and when to suspect an autoimmune etiology over direct toxicity.

blogs.title: Rhabdo or Autoimmune? Differentiating Toxic vs. Immune Necrotizing Myopathy
blogs.description: Not all muscle breakdown is created equal. This case highlights the critical clinical distinctions between drug-induced rhabdomyolysis and immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM). We analyze the time course of CK elevation, the persistence of symptoms after drug withdrawal, and the necessity of immunosuppression to differentiate a direct toxic effect from an autoimmune trigger, guiding appropriate workup and treatment.

blogs.title: Don't Miss the Muscle: AST/ALT Elevation in the Setting of Proximal Weakness
blogs.description: Elevated transaminases often trigger a liver workup, but in patients with muscle weakness, they may be of myopathic origin. This post reviews the patient's history of NAFLD and persistent transaminaemia, teaching how to distinguish hepatic from muscular sources using CK correlation and biopsy findings. We discuss the pitfalls of attributing AST/ALT solely to liver disease in metabolic patients.

blogs.title: Seronegative IMNM: When Antibody Panels Fail and Biopsy Saves the Day
blogs.description: Approximately one-third of patients with immune-mediated necrotising myopathy are seronegative for classic autoantibodies like HMGCR or SRP. This case demonstrates the diagnostic challenge when the myositis panel is negative. We review the histological hallmarks of IMNM—necrotising myofibres, macrophage infiltration, and membrane attack complex staining—and emphasize the role of muscle biopsy in seronegative presentations.

blogs.title: Drug-Induced IMNM: Why This Case Responded Faster Than Idiopathic Myositis
blogs.description: Idiopathic IMNM often requires prolonged, intensive immunosuppression. In contrast, this patient achieved remission with a short course of steroids and IVIG after withdrawing the offending agent. We discuss the management nuances of drug-induced myopathy versus idiopathic disease, including the rationale for rapid steroid weaning and the importance of avoiding re-exposure to the trigger.
